test_title: SSC Selection Post Matric Level Official Paper (Held on: 2 Feb 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: In a 1000 km trip, a man drives at a speed of 50 km/h for the first five-eighth of the total distance. If he completes the whole journey in 19 hours (resting time not included), what is his speed (in km/h, correct up to 1 decimal place) for the rest of the journey?
solution:
**Given:**

Total distance = 1000 km

Speed for 5/8th of the distance = 50 km/h

Total time taken = 19 hours

**Concept used:**

Speed = Distance/time

**Calculation:**

five-eighth of 1000 = 1000 × (5/8)

⇒ 625 km

Remaining distance = 1000 - 625

⇒ 375

Time taken to cover 625 km = 625/50

⇒ 12.5 hours

Remaining time = 19 - 12.5

⇒ 6.5 hours

Speed of the remaining distance = 375/6.5

⇒ 57.69 ≈ 57.7 km/h

**∴ His speed (in km/h, correct up to 1 decimal place) for the rest of the journey was 57.7.**
